specPoints.text: be able to deduce the rate-determining step from a rate equation and vice versa

primer.text: A reaction can only go as fast as its slowest step. The rate-determining step is the slowest stage of a mechanism, and any species taking part in it appears in the rate equation. This note uses that link in both directions: predicting a plausible mechanism from orders, and locating the slow step once the mechanism is known.

lessons.title: The slowest step rules the rate
lessons.opening: A multi-step reaction moves at the pace of its slowest stage. That stage is the rate-determining step, and any species taking part in it earns a place in the rate equation. Reading the rate equation backwards therefore predicts which molecules must collide in the slow step, sketching the mechanism's shape.
keyPoints: In any multi-step reaction the rate-determining step is its slowest stage, and it sets the pace for everything else.
A reactant that appears in the rate-determining step also appears in the rate equation.
The rate equation rate = k[CH3Br][OH-] shows that both CH3Br and OH- take part in the slow step.
For NO2 with CO forming NO and CO2, the rate equation rate = k[NO2]^2 implies two NO2 molecules and zero CO molecules in the rate-determining step.
A compatible mechanism follows: two NO2 react slowly, and the NO3 formed reacts fast with CO.

low.restatement: Species in the slow step appear in the rate equation; powers tell you how many of each are in that step, so the equation sketches the mechanism.
low.analogy: A production line runs at its slowest station's speed; whoever stands at that station is the bottleneck that the output number names.
low.examPointer: State the molecule count in the slow step ('two NO2, zero CO') before writing the mechanism.

medium.restatement: The rate equation is the slow step's attendance register: each power counts the molecules of that species engaged in the bottleneck.
medium.analogy: A bouncer counts heads per group entering; the door log (rate equation) tells you the group sizes at the slow gate.
medium.examPointer: Remember an order can be zero: an absent species may still react, just only in fast later steps.

options.text: The slowest step of the reaction mechanism
options.explanation: Speed of the whole process equals the speed of its slowest stage.

options.text: The first step written on paper
options.explanation: Order of writing does not decide speed.

options.text: The step releasing the most energy
options.explanation: Energy release is not the criterion here.
Catalyst involvement does not define the step.

check.stem: A species appears in the rate equation when it

options.text: Takes part in the rate-determining step
options.explanation: Slow-step participants earn their place in the rate equation.
Fast-step-only species stay out.
Overall-equation presence is not the criterion.
Products generally appear only if they catalyse or inhibit.

check.stem: The rate equation rate = k[CH3Br][OH-] implies that the slow step involves

options.explanation: First order in each means one of each in the slow step.
The power counts molecules; CH3Br is first order.
The OH- factor names it in the slow step too.

options.text: Neither species, since orders are unknown
options.explanation: The equation states both orders plainly.

check.stem: For NO2 with CO, rate = k[NO2]^2 tells us the rate-determining step uses

options.text: Two NO2 molecules and no CO molecules
options.explanation: The square means two; the absence of CO means zero.
CO is zero order, so it is absent from the slow step.
CO's zero order forbids CO in the slow step.
The squared power means two.

check.stem: The compatible two-step mechanism for NO2 with CO has as its slow step

options.explanation: Two NO2 in the slow step matches rate = k[NO2]^2.

options.text: NO3 plus CO giving NO2 and CO2
options.explanation: That is the fast second step.

options.text: CO decomposing to C and O2
options.explanation: No such step appears in the mechanism.
Products do not feed the slow step here.

check.modelAnswer: The slowest step in the reaction mechanism, which sets the overall pace.

check.stem: State what the rate equation rate = k[NO2]^2 implies about CO in the slow step.
check.modelAnswer: CO is zero order, so no CO molecules take part in the rate-determining step.

check.stem: Explain why both CH3Br and OH- in rate = k[CH3Br][OH-] points to their joint presence in the slow step.
check.modelAnswer: Only species engaged in the slow step influence the pace of the whole process, so a species appearing with a positive power in the rate equation must be present in that bottleneck; both names in the equation means both molecules in the slow step.

check.stem: A reaction's rate equation is rate = k[X]^2[Y]^0. Sketch the molecule content of its rate-determining step.
check.modelAnswer: Two molecules of X and none of Y collide in the slow step; Y may participate in fast steps only, which its zero order records.

lessons.title: Locating the slow step in a known mechanism
lessons.opening: Run the logic the other way and the mechanism hands you the slow step. The alkaline bromination of propane carries rate = k[propane][OH-]; since bromine is absent from that equation, the slow step must be the one where propane meets hydroxide, not the later bromine stage.
keyPoints: When the mechanism is known, the rate equation identifies the rate-determining step among the stages.
The alkaline bromination of propane has overall equation CH3CH2CH3 plus Br2 plus OH- forming CH3CH2CH2Br, water and Br-.
Its rate equation is rate = k[CH3CH2CH3][OH-], naming propane and hydroxide as slow-step participants.
Since bromine is absent from the rate equation, Br2 cannot be in the slow step.
The first stage, propane plus OH- giving the carbanion and water, is therefore the rate-determining step.

low.restatement: Match the rate equation's species to the mechanism's steps: the step holding exactly those species is the slow one; missing species (Br2 here) mark fast steps.
low.analogy: Suspects in a line-up: the rate equation's names are the culprits; whichever step's description includes them all is the scene of the crime.
low.examPointer: Use elimination: a species absent from the rate equation cannot be in the slow step.

medium.restatement: The rate equation is a search warrant listing who may be present; each mechanism step is a room, and the slow room is the one whose contents match the warrant exactly.
medium.analogy: Matching a boarding list to airplane seats: the row holding all listed passengers is the one that matters.
medium.examPointer: Quote the absent species explicitly - it is the clue that eliminates the fast step.

check.stem: In the alkaline bromination of propane, bromine's absence from the rate equation shows that

options.text: Br2 is not involved in the rate-determining step
options.explanation: Absent species stay out of the slow step.

options.text: Br2 is not involved in the reaction at all
options.explanation: Bromine appears in the overall equation, so it reacts in fast steps.
No catalytic role is implied.
The equation is exactly informative enough.

check.stem: The rate-determining step of the propane bromination mechanism is

options.text: CH3CH2CH3 plus OH- giving CH3CH2CH2^- plus H2O
options.explanation: Exactly the species the rate equation names.
Bromine's zero order excludes it from the slow step.

options.text: The step forming the final product
options.explanation: Product formation can be fast.
The rate equation identifies it.

check.stem: Identifying a rate-determining step from a mechanism requires

options.text: The mechanism's steps and the rate equation
options.explanation: Matching species across the two locates the slow step.
The overall equation hides the steps.

options.text: The enthalpy change of the reaction
options.explanation: Enthalpy is not the criterion.
Colour is irrelevant here.

check.stem: A proposed mechanism has three steps, and the rate equation names species found only in step two. The rate-determining step is

options.explanation: Species membership in the slow step decides it.

options.text: Step one, because it comes first
options.explanation: Sequence position does not decide speed.

options.text: Step three, because it finishes the reaction
options.explanation: Completion does not decide speed.
The information is exactly sufficient.

check.stem: In the propane bromination mechanism, the intermediate formed in the slow step is

options.text: CH3CH2CH2^-, the carbanion formed when propane loses a proton to hydroxide
options.explanation: The slow step produces the carbanion intermediate.
Bromide is a product of the fast bromination stage.
Water forms in the slow step but is a product there, not an intermediate carried forward.
Bromine is a reactant of a later fast step.

check.stem: State the rate equation for the alkaline bromination of propane.
check.modelAnswer: Rate = k[CH3CH2CH3][OH-], first order in propane and first order in hydroxide.

check.stem: State which species is absent from the slow step of the propane bromination.
check.modelAnswer: Bromine (Br2) is absent from the rate-determining step.

check.stem: Explain how the rate equation locates the rate-determining step in a known mechanism.
check.modelAnswer: The rate equation lists the species whose concentrations govern the pace, and only the slow step involves exactly those species; scanning the mechanism for the step containing all of them, and none of the absent ones, locates the bottleneck.

check.stem: A mechanism has steps: (1) A plus B giving R, slow; (2) R plus C giving product, fast. Write the rate equation.
check.modelAnswer: Rate = k[A][B], because only A and B are present in the rate-determining first step and R is an intermediate.

glossary.definition: The slowest step of a mechanism, whose participants appear in the rate equation.
A species formed in one step and consumed in a later step, never appearing in the rate equation.
The sequence of elementary steps a reaction follows from reactants to products.
